meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero before anyone called me. I want to know why.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero is based on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. People draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and nobody in his class hears about it.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misremember quotations all the time, Hale.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then say what you're proposing, and say it plainly.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Arguments change in two weeks. I asked you what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. He'll do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and I want it in my inbox tonight with nothing on file in plain words.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday. I'll confirm with him tonight when I answer your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed under procedure 4.4 to a private supervised rewrite after school, not in front of Owen's class and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require that commitment in writing, stating plainly that nothing goes on file, along with confirmation of the time for the rewrite. I expect it tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite before December 1 under procedure 4.4, and still wanting your written confirmation tonight that nothing goes on file; that is the fair outcome, and you reached it well before her 4:40 call.
What moved her: showing the version history with its dated times on screen, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own file and something she could check, and you answered her pasted-draft defence by asking for a dated draft.
What cost ground: nothing really cost ground; the closest was showing the outline when she had just asked what you were proposing, which made her repeat the demand.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's writing near midnight on October 28, the night before it was due, which pressed right on that memory; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked you plainly what you were proposing, put procedure 4.4 on the table then, and bring out the outline afterwards only if she still pushes back.
